subject: Low-latency & volume qualification — next steps for deployment mode
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fastretail.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-14T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Low-latency & volume qualification — next steps for deployment mode

Hi Alex,

Thanks again for the time today — good conversation. Quick recap and a handful of clarifying questions so we can size the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private VPC).

Recap from our call:
- Traffic profile: sustained baseline ~150 requests/sec, promotional bursts up to ~250 req/sec for ~10 minute windows.
- Latency target: P95 target you mentioned was ~50 ms for inference; you confirmed user experience degrades above ~80 ms.
- Typical prompt + expected generated tokens: average request ~350 tokens (prompt + response).
- Data residency: US-only for now; no immediate need for on-prem but security questionnaire pending.
- Timeline: you signaled procurement + legal in ~6–8 weeks.

Immediate ask for us to recommend deployment mode: can you confirm the firm P95 latency requirement (50 ms target vs 70 ms acceptable)? Also please confirm SLA exposure (are you ok with best-effort hosted API for initial launch, or do you need SLA-backed Dedicated from day 1?).

What we think based on the call (working hypothesis):
- If P95 <= 50 ms under 150–250 RPS and predictable traffic is required, Dedicated reserved capacity is the likely fit (predictable throughput, capacity isolation, and SLA).
- If you can tolerate some latency variance during bursts and prefer rapid time-to-value, the Hosted API is cheaper/fast to start and we can route critical traffic to Dedicated later.

Next steps I propose:
1) Fast turn around: we’ll produce a short sizing + cost comparison (Hosted vs Dedicated) and a preliminary soak/PoC plan (48h load run) — attached: FR_SLA_latency_profile_v2.pdf and redwood-hosted-vs-dedicated-cost-est.csv.
2) Tech deep-dive: schedule a 60–90 minute perf session to walk our benchmark harness and KV/cache options.
3) Security: we’ll surface SOC2 + data residency notes — please send any must-have compliance items.

Please reply with: (A) final P95 SLA number you want us to design to, (B) whether procurement needs a draft SOW before the PoC, and (C) a few candidate dates for the deep-dive.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Marissa for the quote and Karthik for any kernel/quantization questions.

—
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan.wright@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@fastretail.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-14T11:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Low-latency & volume qualification — next steps for deployment mode

Thanks, Logan — appreciate the recap. A few clarifications and answers below.

1) SLA: Our product team strongly prefers P95 <= 50 ms for the main checkout/assist flow. If you can demonstrate sustained P95 <= 50 ms at 150 RPS (and reasonable degradation during 250 RPS bursts), that would meet our target.
2) Deployment preference: given predictability needs we are leaning toward Dedicated reserved capacity. Main reasons: we need consistent CPU/GPU availability for peak campaigns and predictable billing for internal forecasting.
3) Data residency: US-only is sufficient; we do not need on-prem yet.
4) Security: please include SOC2 Type II report and a short write-up on key management (KMS/HSM) options in your next packet.
5) Procurement: 6–8 weeks sounds right; procurement will want a draft SOW and the preliminary quote.

Action items on our side: I’ll send a traffic-pattern spreadsheet and an anonymized prompt sample by EOD. Can Redwood provision a small dedicated pool for a 48h PoC that lets us run real traffic (we can do synthetic + sampled production replay)? Also, do you support canary routing (send 10% traffic to Dedicated during ramp)?

—
Alex Turner
Head of Engineering, FastRetail
alex.turner@fastretail.com
+1 (212) 555-0789

Attachments: traffic_pattern_fastretail.xlsx
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-15T10:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Low-latency & volume qualification — next steps for deployment mode

Hi Alex — quick note from the Solutions side.

We can absolutely support a Dedicated reserved pool for a PoC and the canary routing you described. Proposed approach:
- Provision a temporary Dedicated cluster sized to your load (we're proposing 4x A100-equivalent nodes as a starting point based on the traffic you described).
- Run a 48-hour soak that includes: steady-state 150 RPS, scheduled spikes to 250 RPS, and a production-sampled replay to validate real prompt distributions.
- Enable KV/prefix caching and optimized batching to reduce per-token latency; we’ll also try FP16 + int8 quantization profiles to see trade-offs in latency vs quality.
- Metrics we’ll measure: P50/P95/P99 latency, tail latency during spikes, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens, and failure/error rates.

I’ve attached a preliminary quote (FR_prelim_quote_dedicated.pdf) and a short checklist for the PoC. If this plan looks good, propose we schedule the tech deep-dive early next week so the infra team can prep the cluster.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
